findings.location: prayerbook_for_the_new_year-heidenheim-1965-he/uvekhen_lekha_taaleh_qedushah.xml, the tei:choice inside the prayer:uvekhen_lekha_taaleh_qedushah/text part, plus the matching selectors in musaf_uvekhen_lekha_taaleh_qedushah.xml (he) and the index and expanded-order callers
findings.problem: On p.59 the parenthesised (הוּא) is a word that some say and others leave out, and p.107 leaves it out. JLPTEI-3 says outright that 'Text that some communities add and others omit is a condition, not an alternate'. It also says that when the source sets a passage off with parentheses, the conditional is @type="marked". Here the whole sentence is instead duplicated as two j:option elements, and the first option has the printed parentheses inside the words to be read. Setting attah_hu_eloheinu=true therefore selects a 'wording' that includes editorial brackets, which nobody says. j:option means 'exactly one of which is read', which does not fit.
findings.fix: Keep one sentence. Wrap only הוּא in <j:conditional type="marked"> with a single condition URN (for example …:condition:prayer:uvekhen_lekha_taaleh_qedushah/text/hu), and leave the parentheses to the marked rendering. The p.107 host and the expanded-order caller declare that condition false. The p.59 caller leaves it undefined, or declares true if the edition's reading is wanted. Change the commentary note's j:condition to test the same feature: true or undefined sets the note, false suppresses it. Then drop the attah_hu_eloheinu/attah_eloheinu option pair.

findings.location: tei:sourceDesc/tei:bibl/tei:biblScope in: en gevurot_parts.xml (16–16), he+en rh_vetimlokh.xml (17–17), en veattah_qadosh_el_na.xml (51–51), he+en uvekhen_lekha_taaleh_qedushah.xml (59–59)
findings.problem: These canonical homes now contain words printed on other pages. The second j:option readings come from p.102/103 (gevurot English), p.103 (Ps 146:10 in he and en, and Ps 22:4 English) and p.107 (Uvekhen in he and en). Each file's source extent still names only its first page. SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME says biblScope carries one entry per printing. As written, the provenance of words that are physically in the file is wrong.
findings.fix: Add a tei:biblScope unit="pages" for each printing whose words the file contains: en gevurot_parts 16, 102 and 103; rh_vetimlokh 17 and 103; en veattah_qadosh_el_na 51 and 103; uvekhen 59 and 107.

findings.problem: The generator puts a space after the end-referenced Ps 22:4 segment, so the encoded text reads 'Israel , O God.' The source reads 'Israel, O God.' (data.json: fragment 1 ends 'Israel', fragment 2 is ', O God.'). Whitespace in mixed content is text. The Hebrew home has the same defect in a milder form: the inserted space plus the leading space of ' אֵל נָא:' makes a double space. The literal hashes only cover data.json, so they cannot catch this. The exact_words check may be normalising whitespace before punctuation.
findings.fix: Do not insert a separator after an end_reference segment when the next fragment already starts with whitespace or punctuation. Emit `</tei:seg><tei:milestone unit="verse"/><tei:milestone unit="chapter"/>, O God.` in English and a single space in Hebrew. Then check the rendered strings with whitespace kept as is.

findings.location: Every inline j:transclude whose target holds j:option: musaf_repetition_gevurot_open/close, musaf_repetition_yimlokh, musaf_repetition_veattah_qadosh, musaf_uvekhen_lekha_taaleh_qedushah, rh_gevurot and repetition_veattah_qadosh, in both languages
findings.problem: JLPTEI-3 §Inclusions says an inline transclusion keeps 'only one' reading of a tei:choice, 'the j:read (qere), or the first j:option'. Read literally, every later occurrence would get the p.16/17/51/59 wording, which is wrong. The supplied execution evidence shows the exporter applies opensiddur:variant before it flattens the text, so the encoding works only because of behaviour the guideline does not describe. A processor that follows the written guideline would produce the wrong words.
findings.fix: Change the JLPTEI-3 paragraph to say that a decided opensiddur:variant selects among j:option before inline flattening, and that the first option is the fallback only when nothing is decided. Alternatively, use external transclusion where the selection matters. Not blocking, given the execution evidence.

findings.location: he+en veattah_qadosh_el_na.xml (`<tei:milestone unit="chapter" n="22"/>`) and he+en rh_vetimlokh.xml (`n="146"`)
findings.problem: A chapter milestone with @n but no @corresp is a terminator under URN-scope rule 3: it opens nothing. A numbered terminator suggests that a chapter scope opens there. JLPTEI-3 says bare terminators carry neither corresp nor n. Giving it a corresp would wrongly claim the whole chapter.
findings.fix: Drop both chapter milestones around the single-verse quotation (the verse URN already names the chapter), or leave them bare without @n.

findings.location: tei:pb ed="1965" n="51" in he+en veattah_qadosh_el_na.xml; tei:pb ed="1965" n="59" in he+en uvekhen_lekha_taaleh_qedushah.xml
findings.problem: Both texts are now printed twice (51/103 and 59/107). Under SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME, a pb in the file holding a text printed more than once takes a second @ed token naming the printing. The veattah home's pb also duplicates the pb 51 in repetition_veattah_qadosh.xml. It sits outside the /text scope, so it is only emitted if someone transcludes the root.
findings.fix: Remove the pb from veattah_qadosh_el_na (the context file already has it). For uvekhen, either qualify the ed token or note that the p.59 printing has no siddur: unit. A bare '1965' is read as a single printing.

findings.problem: @target names the project but @targetEnd does not. Both ends have to resolve to one file. An unqualified end relies on resolver priority to land in the same project.

findings.location: en repetition_veattah_qadosh.xml, en uvekhen_lekha_taaleh_qedushah.xml, en veattah_qadosh_el_na.xml: tei:title

findings.fix: Add xml:lang="he" to the Hebrew titles, or give English titles. Retitle gevurot_parts to describe the text, not the evening context.

findings.location: he+en rh_gevurot.xml and repetition_veattah_qadosh.xml: the host j:declare, plus the identical index caller declare
findings.problem: The same wording selection is declared twice, once at the caller and once in the siddur host. It does no harm, but there are two sources of truth for the default.
findings.fix: Keep one declaration, preferably the caller's, to match the rule that host defaults live at callers.

findings.problem: The idno names only prayer:amidah/gevurot/attah_gibbor, but the file realises four parts.
findings.fix: Use a file-level identifier, or leave the idno out, rather than naming one of the parts.

Verified: the canonical homes (gevurot_parts, veattah_qadosh_el_na, rh_vetimlokh for Ps 146:10, uvekhen for /text) carry no j:declare. Defaults sit at the index callers, and each later host declares its own exact wording using only opensiddur:variant, with no invented day or service flags.

Verified: paragraphing follows each source. On p.102 the Hebrew is one paragraph (one ranged inline transclusion) and the English is two (two transclusions). On p.103 each language is one paragraph.
